questions.q: What is the one axis that separates IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS?
options: Price — IaaS is always cheapest, SaaS always most expensive
How much the customer manages versus how much the provider manages
The physical country where the data center sits
Whether the service uses IPv4 or IPv6
questions.explain: All three models sit on a sliding scale of how much the customer has to manage versus how much the provider manages on their behalf.

questions.q: With IaaS, what does the customer manage themselves?
options: Nothing — the provider manages everything
Only the physical data center
The operating system, runtime, and application, on top of provider-managed VMs, storage, and networking
Only the application's user interface
questions.explain: IaaS hands the customer raw compute, storage, and networking; the customer installs and manages the OS, runtime, and application themselves.

questions.q: What is the key difference between PaaS and IaaS?
options: PaaS has no internet connectivity
With PaaS, the provider also manages the OS and runtime, so the customer just deploys application code
PaaS only runs on-premises
There is no difference — they are the same thing
questions.explain: PaaS goes a step further than IaaS: the provider manages the OS and runtime, so the customer just deploys code with no server to log into or patch.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge Retail run its email and CRM on SaaS products?
options: Because SaaS is always free
Because they need a completely custom, nonstandard OS configuration
Because email and CRM are standard needs well served by a finished application nobody needs to manage the infrastructure for
Because SaaS requires their own physical servers
questions.explain: SaaS fits standard needs where customization isn't required — Northbridge Retail just logs into Microsoft 365 and Salesforce rather than managing any underlying infrastructure.

questions.q: What is the main tradeoff between choosing IaaS versus SaaS for a workload?
options: IaaS offers more flexibility but more operational work; SaaS offers less work but less customization
There is no tradeoff — they perform identically
SaaS is only available for networking equipment
IaaS always costs less money than SaaS
questions.explain: More control (IaaS) comes with more effort to patch, scale, and secure the OS; less control (SaaS) means less effort but less ability to customize what's running underneath.
